newsitem.title: USA: FDIC Chairman-credit card banks no threat to FDIC.
newsitem.headline: FDIC Chairman-credit card banks no threat to FDIC.

text.p: The chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation told the U.S. House Banking Committee Thursday that the 77 banks holding roughly two-thirds of the nation's credit card debt pose no threat to funds in the FDIC.
"A number of factors suggest that, overall, credit card banks do not currently pose a threat to the deposit insurance funds," said FDIC Chairman Ricki Helfer in prepared testimony.
She said nearly two-thirds of all credit card loans outstanding at FDIC-insured institutions are held by 77 banks specializing in credit card lending.
But she cautioned that there could be problems in the future because the FDIC's losses are determined by the performance of the individual banks.
"Individual institutions could encounter problems in the future. The FDIC is closely following their conditions and performance," Helfer said.
